1.d4 d5 2.c4 Nc6 3.Nc3 e6 4.Nf3.strategy: Develops and guards d4 against the knight on c6, so White simply continues development and keeps its central pawns intact. Black has played a solid move that does not solve the problem of the awkward knight on c6.

1.d4 d5 2.c4 Nc6 3.Nc3 e6 4.Nf3 Nf6.strategy: Brings the king's knight to its natural square and guards e4, reaching the set-up of a declined gambit with the queen's knight already on c6. Sound and natural, but that knight blocks the c-pawn, so Black has less than the usual counterplay in the centre.
